title: Exact mobility rings in non-Hermitian quasiperiodically decorated Lieb lattices
authors: Ming-Jie Tao, Yi-Ting Wang, Jing Li, Hongsheng Hou, Xiang-Ping Jiang, Lei Pan
abstract: The mobility ring (MR), a critical boundary in the complex energy plane separating extended and localized states, is fundamental to understanding the Anderson transition in non-Hermitian (NH) disordered systems. While MRs have been extensively studied in one-dimensional (1D) NH quasiperiodic models, rigorous analytical frameworks beyond 1D remain critically scarce. Here, we investigate a class of two-dimensional (2D) quasiperiodically decorated Lieb lattices (QDLLs) featuring complex incommensurate potentials selectively applied to the lattice vertices. By exactly mapping these 2D structures onto NH generalized Aubry-Andr{é}-Harper (AAH) models and leveraging extended-localized transition point, we analytically derive the Lyapunov exponents and obtain exact expressions for the MRs. These exact theoretical boundaries are strongly corroborated by numerical computations of wavefunction fractal dimensions and real-space probability distributions. Furthermore, we reveal distinct evolutionary behaviors of the MRs driven by the quasiperiodic potential strength: systems characterized by $κ=2$ possess a single MR, whereas systems with $κ=3$ undergo a dynamic sequential evolution from a single integrated ring into two independent rings. We hope that our exact results of MRs in 2D will benefit the study of Anderson localizations and MRs in high-dimensional NH systems.
summary: The paper analytically determines the Mobility Rings in complex two-dimensional quasiperiodic lattices by mapping them onto effective Aubry-André-Harper models. It establishes that these rings define the boundary between extended and localized electronic states, revealing a fascinating topological transition where the ring splits into multiple components depending on the lattice's decoration parameter.
main_problem: The study focuses on understanding the mobility ring (MR), a critical boundary separating extended and localized states, particularly in non-Hermitian disordered systems beyond one dimension.
main_result: The authors derived exact analytical expressions for the MRs in 2D quasiperiodically decorated Lieb lattices, revealing that the topology of this ring evolves dynamically based on the lattice decoration parameter $\kappa$ (e.g., splitting into two rings when $\kappa=3$).
method: The methodology involves exactly mapping the complex 2D structure onto an effective generalized Aubry-André-Harper model, followed by analytical derivation of Lyapunov exponents and utilizing transfer matrix formalisms.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional (2D) quasiperiodically decorated Lieb lattice (QDLL) incorporating complex incommensurate potentials. The analysis uses the tight-binding Hamiltonian projected onto vertex sites, which is then mapped to an effective 1D/2D AAH model.
key_observables: Mobility Ring (MR), Lyapunov exponents (LEs), wavefunction fractal dimension ($\Gamma$), and real-space probability distributions.
important_parameters: $V$ (modulation amplitude), $\theta$ (complex phase factor), $\kappa$ (decoration parameter, e.g., 2 or 3), and incommensurate frequencies $\alpha_{x,y}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes $t=1$ (unit energy) and fixes specific irrational values for the modulation frequencies ($\alpha_x = \alpha_y = (\sqrt{5}-1)/2$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the conceptual phase diagram showing the MR boundary, structural representations of the lattice, and plots detailing the evolution of the MR topology (e.g., single ring vs. two sub-rings) as a function of potential strength $V$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the physical system and Hamiltonian, developing an exact mapping to an effective AAH model using algebraic decimation, analytically deriving the critical conditions for the MRs via Lyapunov exponents, and finally demonstrating the topological phase transitions observed numerically.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous analytical benchmarks in 2D non-Hermitian systems, which is crucial for understanding localization phenomena that are difficult to treat theoretically beyond 1D. The connection between topology (MR splitting) and lattice structure ($\kappa$) is highly relevant for designing synthetic quantum materials.
